I am 63 years old this year. I have been farming since I was in my thirties, and I never went to school. I cannot read, but I know my land. My family has 14 mu of land, and there are only two of us at home now. We have a well, so I can pump water when the sky does not give rain.

I plant 10 mu in the wheat-maize rotation and keep 4 mu for cotton. Cotton is too much work, but it brings good money when the price is right. Last year I had 5 mu of cotton, but my back hurts more now, so I gave 1 mu back to the wheat-maize cycle. Two people cannot manage too much cotton.

**My wheat** — I sowed it last autumn after the corn came out. I used the rotary tiller to turn the stubble under, then I spread the fertilizer and sowed the seed. I use the same improved variety as my neighbor Old Wang — his wheat always looks good. For fertilizer, I put one bag of compound fertilizer on each mu at sowing, that is 50 kg. Then when the wheat turns green in spring, I top-dress with half a bag of urea per mu, about 25 kg. At the jointing stage I put another 15 kg of urea. I would rather put a little too much than too little. A bad harvest means no money for the whole year; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost. I irrigate three times: once when it greens up, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. I spray pesticide three times — herbicide once and insecticide twice when I see aphids. I expect about 1000 jin per mu, same as last year.

**My maize** — After the wheat comes out in early June, there is no time to waste. I hire the machine to sow maize directly into the wheat stubble, no-tillage. I use hybrid seed, the kind with the big ears. I put about 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at sowing, and when the plants reach knee-high — the big trumpet stage — I spread another 20 kg of urea per mu. I irrigate twice: once if it is dry right after sowing, and once at the big trumpet stage. I spray herbicide once and insecticide twice. I expect about 1100 jin per mu, maybe 550 kg. That is what I usually get.

**My cotton** — Cotton is trouble, but I know how to do it. In spring I plough the 4 mu deep and lay the plastic film. I use an improved cotton seed. I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, about 50 kg. When the plants flower, I top-dress with urea, about 25 kg per mu. Cotton needs potassium, so I add a little potash fertilizer too, maybe 8 kg per mu. I irrigate three times — at planting if dry, at flowering, and when the bolls are forming. I spray pesticide many times, maybe 10 times. The bollworms and aphids never stop. Last year I sprayed more than 10 times. If I see one bug, I spray. I expect about 550 jin of seed cotton per mu, about 275 kg.

Everything costs money. Fertilizer is expensive this year. But I watched Old Zhang across the road — he is cutting back on fertilizer to save money. I think he is foolish. I will do what I did last year, maybe a little more. I have been doing this for 30 years. I know my land.
